'''Christof Paar''' (born July 18, 1963, in [[Cologne]]) is a [[Germany|German]] [[Cryptography|cryptographer]]. He is one of the founding directors at the Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy in [[Bochum]], Germany, a "Scientific Member" of the [[Max Planck Society]],<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Christof Paar |url=https://www.mpi-sp.org/paar |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy}}</ref> [[IEEE Fellow]],<ref name="auto1">{{Cite journal |title=Member Awards, Fellows, and Call for Nominations |journal=IEEE Signal Processing Magazine|date=2011 |volume=28 |issue=2 | doi=10.1109/MSP.2011.940238 }}</ref> and a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=List of Members – Expert Search |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/christof-paar/ |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Leopoldina – Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
After training as a telecommunications technician, Christof Paar studied telecommunication engineering at the [[Cologne University of Applied Sciences]] (then [[FH Köln]]) from 1984 to 1988. After his [[Alternative civilian service|civilian service]], he studied [[electrical engineering]] with a specialization in computer technology at the University of Siegen from 1989 to 1991. He wrote his diploma thesis at [[Michigan Technological University]] on active noise control.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae Prof. Dr. Christof Paar |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Christof_Paar_D.pdf |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Leopoldina – Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften}}</ref> From 1991 to 1994, he was a doctoral student with [[A.J. Han Vinck|Han Vinck]] at the Institute for Experimental Mathematics at the [[University of Duisburg-Essen]] (then the [[University of Essen]]).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr.-Ing. Christof Paar – Curriculum Vitae |url=https://www.mpg.de/15153658/security-and-privacy-paar |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft}}</ref> His dissertation was on computer architectures for arithmetic in [[Finite field arithmetic|finite fields]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paar, C., 1994. Effiziente VLSI-Architekturen für bit-parallele Arithmetik in endlichen Körpern. Inst. für Experimentelle Mathematik. |url=https://portal.dnb.de/opac/showFullRecord?currentResultId=auRef%3D1032727705%26any&currentPosition=8#:~:text=Titel%20Efficient%20VLSI%20architectures%20for,1994 |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Deutsche Nationalbibliothek}}</ref> From 1995 to 2001, he was an assistant and later an associate professor at [[Worcester Polytechnic Institute]] in [[Massachusetts]] for nearly seven years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=20 Years of Crypto - Cryptography and Data Security Symposium Honors Two Decades of Innovation |url=https://www.wpi.edu/news/20-years-crypto |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Worcester Polytechnic Institute|date=25 October 2016 }}</ref> From 2001 to 2019, he held the Chair of Embedded Security at [[Ruhr University Bochum]], Germany. From 2008 to 2009 and from 2014 to 2016, he worked as a Research Professor at the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Christof Paar - Affiliated Professor, Electrical and Computer Engineering |url=https://www.umass.edu/engineering/about/directory/christof-paar |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=University of Massachusetts Amherst}}</ref> Since 2019, he is one of the two founding directors of the new [[Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy]] in Bochum.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Two elite researchers for IT security and data protection |url=https://www.mpi-sp.org/5655/news_publication_13417859_transferred?c=6054 |access-date=2025-02-10 |website=Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy}}</ref>

Paar's research deals with the engineering aspects of cryptography. He has significantly contributed to efficient implementing [[Symmetric-key algorithm|symmetric]] and [[Public-key cryptography|asymmetric crypto]] algorithms, [[Side-channel attack|side-channel analysis]], embedded systems security, and [[hardware security]].<ref name="auto"/> In 1999, he co-founded, with Çetin Koç, [[CHES]] (Conference on Cryptographic Hardware and Embedded Systems) at [[Worcester Polytechnic Institute|WPI]], which has become one of the leading international conferences on cryptography.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Steering Committee |url=https://ches.iacr.org/steeringcommittee.php |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=CHES }}</ref> At [[Ruhr University Bochum]], he established the [[Horst Görtz Institute for Information Security]] together with [[Hans Dobbertin]] and was instrumental in building Bochum's bachelor's and master's degree programs in the field of IT security.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Historie |url=https://hgi.rub.de/en/ |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security}}</ref> Since 2019, he is co-spokesperson for the Cluster of Excellence "CASA - Cyber Security in the Age of Large-Scale Attackers", together with Eike Kiltz and Angela Sasse.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Christof Paar – Embedded Security |url=https://www.mpi-sp.org/paar |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy}}</ref> In 2003, Paar founded Escrypt GmbH together with Willi Mannheims, one of the first companies to focus on industrial data security. Since 2012, Escrypt has been part of [[Robert Bosch GmbH]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Christof Paar in der Leopoldina |url=https://hgi.rub.de/news/newsarchiv/hgi/christof-paar-in-der-leopoldina |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Horst-Görtz-Institut für IT-Sicherheit|date=5 July 2019 }}</ref>

* 2013 DHL Innovation Award (mit Gregor Leander und Axel Poschmann)<ref>{{Cite web |title=IT-Sicherheit zum kleinen Preis |url=https://idw-online.de/de/news530556 |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Informationsdienst Wissenschaft e. V.}}</ref>

* 2021 Ring of honor of the city of Bochum<ref>{{Cite web |title=15 Persönlichkeiten erhalten Ehrenring der Stadt Bochum".
